macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Global equities rebound as AI fears ease
items.summary: European equities rallied, with the Stoxx 600 up 1.8%, the DAX up 2.1%, the Euro Stoxx 50 up 2%, and the FTSE 100 up 1.8%. U.S. stock futures also rose after Thanksgiving as the AI-driven selloff showed signs of stabilizing.[4][6]

items.title: Asian stocks extend recovery; South Korean shares surge
items.summary: The Hang Seng rose 1.19%, ending a seven-session losing streak, while the KOSPI gained 4.34% to 4,915.68. Market sentiment improved amid expectations of additional Chinese support and a rebound in technology shares.[1][5][7]

items.title: U.S. growth and inflation data strengthen hawkish Fed outlook
items.summary: Third-quarter U.S. GDP growth was revised to an annualized 4.3% from 3.4%, while October headline PCE inflation reached 3.8% year over year and core PCE accelerated to 3.3%. The data reinforce expectations that the Federal Reserve will maintain a restrictive stance and could raise rates in December.[3][9]

items.title: Bank of Korea raises policy rate to 3.25%
items.summary: The Bank of Korea increased its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to 3.25%, reportedly seeking to support the South Korean won. The move adds to a broader pattern of divergent central-bank policy across Asia.[1]

items.title: Bank of Japan signals possible December rate hike
items.summary: Bank of Japan executive director Naoki Tamura said the central bank should move policy toward a neutral rate and discuss another increase in December or later. Expectations for a December hike rose as Japan’s underlying CPI was reported at 3.5% year over year.[4][6]

items.title: ECB minutes maintain possibility of another rate increase
items.summary: Accounts of the European Central Bank’s October deliberations showed that many officials considered another rate hike necessary unless the inflation outlook improved significantly.[6]

items.title: Oil prices climb above $97 as geopolitical concerns intensify
items.summary: Brent crude rose above $97 a barrel as Middle East tensions increased, adding to inflation and growth concerns even as risk appetite returned in global equity markets.[4]

items.title: Macquarie Bank names new chief executive amid restructuring
items.summary: Macquarie Group announced a restructuring of its banking division and said Amy Mahony will succeed Stuart Green as chief executive of Macquarie Bank.[8]

items.title: Imperial Brands jumps on potential Altria bid
items.summary: Imperial Brands shares surged 13.3% after Altria said it was considering a potential all-cash offer for the British tobacco company.[8]

items.title: Dell reports major earnings beat
items.summary: Dell Technologies reportedly posted fiscal third-quarter earnings per share of $9.45, well above analyst expectations of $6.56, driven by stronger revenue and margins in its Infrastructure Solutions Group.[9]

items.title: AI and semiconductor stocks remain central to market volatility
items.summary: Technology shares continued to drive global market swings, with investors rotating out of and back into AI-related stocks. Upcoming results from Broadcom, Micron, and Oracle are expected to provide further signals on AI infrastructure demand.[1][7]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin ETF outflows continue as BTC trades near $60,000
items.summary: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded about $453 million in net outflows, extending the losing streak to seven sessions. Bitcoin was broadly stable, trading near $60,000, while Zcash fell roughly 9% and Monero dropped about 10–11%.

items.title: Switzerland launches first spot Bitcoin ETF
items.summary: Switzerland’s first spot Bitcoin ETF began trading on the SIX Swiss Exchange, initially holding about 350 BTC and charging an annual fee of 0.19%.

items.title: Over $600 million in stolen Binance-linked assets moved through THORChain
items.summary: Researchers reported that more than $600 million in cryptocurrency stolen in a Binance-related hack was routed through THORChain, with additional funds allegedly sent through mixing services and North Korean hackers blamed.

items.title: U.S. Bitcoin reserve bill advances toward House vote
items.summary: The proposed American Reserve Modernization Act of 2026 would require the U.S. government to hold Bitcoin for at least 20 years without selling it.

items.title: Japan considers tighter rules for DeFi and self-custody wallets
items.summary: Japan’s financial regulator published discussion materials examining possible oversight of decentralized-finance interfaces and unhosted cryptocurrency wallets.

items.title: BNB Chain outlines new Layer-1 network
items.summary: BNB Chain released a whitepaper for a separate Layer-1 blockchain aimed at high-frequency trading, payments, privacy-focused finance and autonomous AI agents, with a public testnet targeted for early 2027.

items.title: Solana introduces platform for blockchain-enabled AI agents
items.summary: Solana launched solana.ai, a developer platform intended to help autonomous AI agents conduct transactions, manage wallets and purchase online services.

items.title: Zodia Custody discloses client-data breach
items.summary: Standard Chartered-backed crypto custodian Zodia Custody reported a security incident that exposed client and staff names and email addresses.

items.title: CFTC allows qualifying crypto assets in reserve calculations
items.summary: CFTC guidance reportedly allows regulated derivatives firms and clearinghouses to count Bitcoin, Ether and qualifying payment stablecoins toward financial-resource requirements, subject to a 20% haircut.

items.title: Ethereum Glamsterdam upgrade gets December test date
items.summary: Ethereum’s Glamsterdam upgrade is scheduled for testing on the Hoodi testnet on December 15.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: US–China chip restrictions threaten Chinese AI model releases
items.summary: Tighter US restrictions on advanced chips and overseas computing are reportedly causing Chinese AI companies to delay major model launches. The developments highlight how compute access is shaping the global AI competition.[1]

items.title: New benchmark evaluates multi-user voice agents
items.summary: Researchers introduced μ-Bench, a benchmark designed to test whether AI voice agents can handle simultaneous, interdependent requests from multiple users in shared environments.[2]

items.title: PROVE targets collusion among AI verification agents
items.summary: A new reinforcement-learning method called PROVE aims to reduce collusion between language-model agents that verify one another during long-running interactions.[1]

items.title: Anthropic expands AI-for-science partnerships
items.summary: Anthropic is expanding its AI for Science program through collaborations involving 20 scientific foundations, institutions and research groups.[1]

items.title: AI referrals to retailers more than double during holiday shopping
items.summary: Traffic to online retail sites from links in AI-powered tools reportedly more than doubled in November compared with the same period in 2025, according to Adobe Digital Insights data cited by the Associated Press.[1]

items.title: FrontierPhysics leaderboard ranks leading AI models
items.summary: Artificial Analysis launched a 54-task physics leaderboard, with Claude Fable 5.2 reportedly leading at 32%, ahead of GPT-6.2 Astra.[7]

items.title: Perplexity launches historical web-search capability
items.summary: Perplexity reportedly launched Time Machine for its Search API and Context API, allowing users to query stored web copies from selected points within the previous year.[7]

items.title: New open models target video audio, image upscaling and document OCR
items.summary: Recently highlighted open-source releases include MAGI-2-preview for adding sound to short videos, Kandinsky ImageSR 2.0 for image upscaling, and OCRia-1 for reading tables, charts and layouts in document images.[7]

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Valve releases Proton 11.0-3 with SteamOS and Linux fixes
items.summary: Valve released Proton 11.0-3, adding compatibility improvements and bug fixes for games running through SteamOS and Linux.

items.title: CD Projekt confirms simultaneous multi-platform launch for The Witcher 4
items.summary: CD Projekt Red said The Witcher 4 will launch at the same time on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S and PC despite a new Sony marketing agreement.

items.title: Ubisoft cuts 166 jobs in Montreal and Quebec City
items.summary: Ubisoft announced 166 job cuts across its Montreal and Quebec City studios as part of ongoing restructuring and changing production priorities.

items.title: Atari Homebrew Awards suspended over AI-assisted development
items.summary: The Atari Homebrew Awards were suspended after organizers said the growth of generative-AI-assisted game development made fair judging more difficult.

items.title: Germany funds three women’s national esports teams
items.summary: Germany’s federal government is providing €200,000 to support the creation of women’s national teams in League of Legends, VALORANT and EA Sports FC.

items.title: Marvel Rivals opens 12 partner-team applications
items.summary: NetEase opened applications for 12 Marvel Rivals Ignite 2027 partner slots, offering top-tier league access, in-game team bundles and revenue sharing.

items.title: Counter-Strike 2 wins Esports Game of the Year
items.summary: Counter-Strike 2 was named Esports Game of the Year at the Esports Awards in Miami.

items.title: Digimon Alysion launches worldwide
items.summary: Digimon Alysion launched globally after surpassing 450,000 pre-registrations.

items.title: Demon Tides dated for January 2027
items.summary: Demon Tides will release on PlayStation 5, Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 on January 21, 2027.

items.title: Pokémon Champions adds 24 Pokémon in December update
items.summary: Pokémon Champions’ December 2 update will add 24 Pokémon and four Mega Evolutions to competitive play under Regulation M-D.

items.title: Esports Nations Cup announces 2027 qualification pathway
items.summary: The Esports Nations Cup announced new qualification tournaments for countries and territories that did not qualify for the 2026 event.
